title: An actual Gaussian joint-data risk has a first variation
source_anchor: Samplinglib original mathematical supplement v1, 2026-10-20; units[4] and its complete formula proof
target_statement: Let P be an actual probability law on E×ℝ, where E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure. Assume only that its input marginal is the standard Gaussian and its actual response coordinate Y is square-integrable. Let p be any finite real polynomial. For any probability ρ on the unit sphere define fρ(x)=∫p(⟨w,x⟩) dρ(w), F(ρ)=∫(fρ(x)−y)² dP(x,y), and Vρ(w)=2∫(fρ(x)−y)p(⟨w,x⟩) dP(x,y). Every squared loss is integrable, and every displayed inner residual-feature product is integrable at every unit direction. For any two parameter probabilities ρ₀,ρ₁, Vρ₀ is integrable under both laws. The actual scalar risk along (1−t)ρ₀+tρ₁ has right derivative ∫Vρ₀ dρ₁−∫Vρ₀ dρ₀ at zero, and F(ρ₁)≥F(ρ₀)+∫Vρ₀ dρ₁−∫Vρ₀ dρ₀.
